long_biography.plain_text:
Reinhard Wirtgen founded a road-building contractor that evolved into a global construction-equipment group. After his death in 1997, sons Jürgen and Stefan became joint managing partners. Jürgen oversaw the Americas, Africa and part of Europe, while Stefan led Asia, Australia and the remaining European markets. Together they broadened the machinery portfolio and international network.

The brothers agreed to sell the group to Deere & Company in 2017, choosing an industrial buyer they believed could preserve its brands, workforce and customer focus. They subsequently built Wirtgen Invest to manage the family capital across real estate, renewable energy, venture holdings and financial markets. Jürgen has described an in-house investment model designed to retain core expertise and support long-term ownership.

Contemporary reporting distinguishes their former geographic remits, but current family-office materials usually speak collectively. The dossier therefore preserves joint leadership without assigning every current investment decision to Jürgen individually or assuming equal ownership percentages.

The definitive agreement was announced in June 2017, and Deere's SEC-filed annual report confirms completion in December 2017. Contemporary figures distinguish the EUR 4.357 billion equity purchase price from an approximately EUR 4.6 billion total transaction value including assumed debt and other consideration. The biographies use only the completed year and omit volatile currency conversions.

Forbes currently reports age 61, while older business articles provide age references at their publication dates. These do not establish a unique birth date or fully consistent birth year under the proposal standard, so no missing birth field is proposed.

Forbes directly describes inheritance from founder Reinhard, while contemporaneous sources establish that Jürgen and Stefan materially expanded the operating business over two decades. Inherited and expanded therefore captures both mechanisms without treating their mother's reported historical shareholding as proof of a particular transfer percentage.

The original construction-equipment business belongs to Deere. Wirtgen Invest now spans unrelated real estate, energy, venture and financial portfolios, with no demonstrated single dominant asset class, so Finance & Investments is more precise than preserving the origin sector or selecting one portfolio vertical.
